segments.speaker: Jekaterina Novikova
segments.text: Okay, so hello and welcome to another episode of the Women in AI Research podcast. I'm your host. And as usual, I'm joined today by Malikeh, my co-host. And today we have the privilege of speaking with Dr. Angelica Lim. Angelica is a computer scientist, researcher and roboticist.

segments.speaker: Jekaterina Novikova
segments.text: She was named as one of five people building the AI future by Forbes, otherwise she's known for her work in the field of Artificial Intelligence and the Social Robotics. Right now she's an Assistant Professor in Computing Science at the Simon Fraser University in Vancouver, Canada, and she's focusing primarily on developing interactive, socially intelligent robots to enhance human-robot interaction. Much of her work explores emotional and cognitive development in robots and how it affects their interactions with humans, with people. She leads the ROSIE lab.

segments.speaker: Angelica Lim
segments.text: Thanks for having me.

segments.speaker: Jekaterina Novikova
segments.text: That's the social robotics lab at the Simon Fraser University. And she builds AI software for robots to interact with the social intelligence and empathy. So welcome to our podcast, Angelica.

segments.speaker: Jekaterina Novikova
segments.text: As you may know, one of the goal of this podcast is to show how diverse is the field of AI research and because of that I want to start with this question today as well. Could you please tell us a little bit about your cultural heritage and where you have spent different parts of your career journey, of your life, including your studies, work, academic career?

segments.speaker: Angelica Lim
segments.text: Sure, it's a bit of a windy road. So my parents are both born and raised in the Philippines and they eventually emigrated in their 20s to the United States where I was born in California. And I lived in the States until I was about 10 and moved to Vancouver for high school and my undergrad in computing science.

segments.speaker: Angelica Lim
segments.text: And so during that time I specialized in AI and I learned a little bit about robotics. I competed in some competitions as some roboticists do. And I eventually decided to do my grad studies in the place at the time - this was the late 2000s - in Japan because at that time I just saw all these great robots coming out on YouTube, and there were these Japanese robots and I was not disappointed. When I got to Japan, there were robots everywhere and I was able to do six years of grad studies there studying robots before continuing on my dream to work on socially interactive robots. And at the time it was being developed as a joint venture between this French company called Aldebaran Robotics and Softbank in Tokyo. So I worked for a little bit in Tokyo and then I moved to Paris for three years before coming back from industry to academia where I am now.

segments.text: That's great.

It's highly interactive because not only are you synchronizing with one person, you're synchronizing with two people. And we made it a multimodal system because we wanted the robot to synchronize with the drummer, but also recognize my cues as a human. segments.speaker: Angelica Lim
